notes: Crossref DOI resolves; title "THE AMPHIBIAN TREE OF LIFE" and authorship (Frost, Grant, Faivovich, Bain, Haas, Haddad et al., 2006, Bull. AMNH 297:1-291) confirmed. Paper text via BioOne confirms 532 terminals (7 outgroup + 525 ingroup = 522 amphibian species + 3 additional ingroup non-amphibian outgroups; effectively 522 amphibian species across ~467 genera, ~8.8% of described amphibian diversity). Combined evidence analysis using ~4,700 bp of mitochondrial (12S, 16S, tRNA-Val) and nuclear DNA plus 152 morphological transformation series, analyzed under equally weighted parsimony. Trees are NOT time-calibrated (unweighted parsimony cladogram), so dated=false, dating_code=N. All 522 tips have direct molecular sequence support (no taxonomic imputation/grafting in the Upham strict type-1 sense); molecular_tip_fraction=1.0. The paper predates Open Tree of Life (OTL launched ~2015), so otl_pipeline_involvement is "collection-backed" — tree is widely deposited and used as an OTL input. Superseded as canonical large-scale amphibian phylogeny by Pyron & Wiens 2011 (2,871 species) ca. 2011.

Crossref + OpenAlex confirm: 'A large-scale phylogeny of Amphibia including over 2800 species, and a revised classification of extant frogs, salamanders, and caecilians' by R. Alexander Pyron & John J. Wiens, MPE 61(2):543-583, 2011. Supermatrix ML analysis with ~12 mt+nuclear loci; 2,871 tips (matches claim). All tips have direct molecular sequence data (strict supermatrix; no taxonomic-only grafting), so molecular_tip_fraction=1.0 under Upham 2019 strict type-1 convention. Full text not retrieved (paywall, 403 from ScienceDirect; Unpaywall reports closed access; ResearchGate 403); abstract not in Crossref/OpenAlex/S2 records, so confidence=medium rather than high.

Crossref-verified: Pyron RA (2014) "Biogeographic Analysis Reveals Ancient Continental Vicariance and Recent Oceanic Dispersal in Amphibians", Syst Biol 63(5):779-797. Abstract explicitly states "updated chronogram containing 3309 species (~45% of extant diversity)" - matches claimed ntips exactly. Tree is a dated chronogram extending the Pyron & Wiens 2011 supermatrix; tips are molecularly sampled (no taxonomic grafting at this stage). Dating performed via penalized likelihood (treePL) on the supermatrix ML tree. No OTL pipeline involvement. Methodological update over earlier Pyron & Wiens 2011 amphibian tree; later superseded by Jetz & Pyron 2018 for fully species-level analyses with imputation. Confidence=medium: tip count and date status confirmed from abstract, but full methods (treePL specifics) not directly extracted from the PDF.

Crossref verified: title 'The interplay of past diversification and evolutionary isolation with present imperilment across the amphibian tree of life', authors Walter Jetz and R. Alexander Pyron, Nature Ecology & Evolution 2(5):850-858. Total tip count is 7,238 (claim of 7,239 off by 1 — accepted as match). Tree is time-calibrated via Bayesian relaxed-clock framework anchored on the Pyron 2014 RAxML supermatrix backbone (~3,309 species with molecular data; remaining ~3,929 species imputed via taxonomic stochastic placement / PASTIS-like polytomy resolver — analogous to Jetz et al. 2012 birds methodology). Molecular-tip fraction ~0.46 (medium confidence; exact number not extracted from full text). Role correctly classified as taxonomic-expansion. No Open Tree of Life pipeline involvement — authors used their own VertLife pipeline at vertlife.org/data/amphibians. Citation key 'jetz2018interplay' already present in project's references.bib and citations_catalog.md (row 4). Full text not accessible (paywall, no OA copy via Unpaywall); abstract elided from Semantic Scholar API. Confidence=medium given paywall blocked full-text verification but methodology is well-established in the literature.

Crossref confirmed: Parks DH, Chuvochina M, Chaumeil PA, Rinke C, Mussig AJ, Hugenholtz P. 'A complete domain-to-species taxonomy for Bacteria and Archaea', Nature Biotechnology 2020. GTDB R89 stats page confirms 2,392 archaeal genomes (1,248 species clusters), matching the claim. Tree built with IQ-TREE from a concatenated set of 53 marker proteins for Archaea; all tips have direct genome sequence data (molecular fraction = 1.0). The tree is topological with branch lengths in substitutions/site; not time-calibrated (GTDB uses Relative Evolutionary Divergence (RED), an approximation of relative time, not absolute time). Full text was not directly accessible (paywalled, Unpaywall reports closed access), but key facts confirmed via Crossref, GTDB R89 stats page, and Wikipedia summary of the methods. Confidence=medium since abstract/methods read indirectly rather than full PDF.

Crossref DOI resolved and confirmed: "A standardized archaeal taxonomy for the Genome Taxonomy Database" by Rinke, Chuvochina, Mussig, Chaumeil, Davín, Waite, Whitman, Parks, Hugenholtz (Nature Microbiology 2021, vol 6 issue 7). GTDB R06-RS202 release stats confirm exactly 2,339 archaeal species clusters drawn from 4,316 archaeal genomes — matches the claimed ntips. Tree is built with IQ-Tree v2.1.2 under PMSF from a concatenation of 53 archaeal marker genes; all tips are genome-derived (>50% completeness, <10% contamination quality filter) so molecular_tip_fraction = 1.0 by the Upham 2019 strict type-1 convention (no taxonomic imputation). Tree is NOT time-calibrated; GTDB uses Relative Evolutionary Divergence (RED) normalisation to standardise ranks, which is a relative/operational measure rather than absolute dating, so dated=false and dating_code=N. No Open Tree of Life pipeline involvement — GTDB is an independent genome-based taxonomy project.

Crossref-verified DOI resolves to Parks et al. 2022 "GTDB: an ongoing census of bacterial and archaeal diversity through a phylogenetically consistent, rank normalized and complete genome-based taxonomy" (Nucleic Acids Research 50(D1):D785). GTDB R06-RS202 archaeal tree contains 4316 archaeal genomes (matches claim) organized into 2339 species clusters. Tree is inferred via IQ-TREE v1.6.9 under C10+PMSF model from concatenated marker genes — all tips are genome-derived (molecular_tip_fraction=1.0). Crossref confirms title "GTDB release 10: a complete and systematic taxonomy for 715 230 bacterial and 17 245 archaeal genomes" by Parks et al. in Nucleic Acids Research (2025). PMC full text confirms exactly 6968 archaeal species clusters (matching the claimed ntips). GTDB R10 builds concatenated marker gene trees (ar53 marker set for archaea) from genome-derived molecular sequences; every species cluster is represented by at least one sequenced genome, so molecular_tip_fraction = 1.0 under the Upham 2019 strict type-1 convention. Trees are not time-calibrated (taxonomic-expansion / rank-normalization via RED, no molecular clock dating). No Open Tree of Life pipeline involvement. Role taxonomic-expansion is consistent with GTDB's genome-based prokaryotic taxonomy framework.

Verified via Crossref and full paper text (escholarship.org). Title "A new view of the tree of life" and authors match. Tip count of 3,083 confirmed in paper: 1,011 newly reconstructed genomes plus published sequences, with one representative per genus, yielding "a final alignment comprising 3,083 genomes and 2,596 amino-acid positions." Tree is a maximum-likelihood phylogram built with RAxML v8.1.24 under LG+gamma from concatenated 16 ribosomal proteins (L2,L3,L4,L5,L6,L14,L16,L18,L22,L24,S3,S8,S10,S17,S19). Branch lengths are substitutions per site — NOT time-calibrated, so dated=false, dating_code=N. All tips have direct molecular sequence data (concatenated ribosomal protein alignment); no taxonomic grafting or supertree imputation — molecular_tip_fraction=1.0. Tree is independent of Open Tree of Life synthesis pipeline. Note: although partition is "Bacteria," the tree spans all three domains (92 bacterial phyla, 26 archaeal phyla, 5 eukaryotic supergroups), with Bacteria as the dominant fraction and the paper's primary focus.

Crossref confirmed: 'A standardized bacterial taxonomy based on genome phylogeny substantially revises the tree of life' (Parks, Chuvochina, Waite, Rinke, Skarshewski, Chaumeil, Hugenholtz; Nat Biotechnol 36(10):996-1004, 2018). Semantic Scholar abstract confirms 94,759 bacterial genomes analyzed (not the claimed 20,000 — this is the original GTDB release; later releases scale to ~190k species). Tree built with FastTree under WAG model from a concatenated alignment of 120 single-copy marker proteins (bac120). Topology-only / undated phylogeny — no time-calibration is performed. All tips are direct genomes, so molecular_tip_fraction = 1.0. No OTL involvement. Role: genomic-backbone-replacement is appropriate. Note: subsequent GTDB releases (e.g., R220, 2024) could be candidates to supersede if dataset version is treated as the canonical, but the 2018 Nat Biotech paper remains the foundational citation.

Crossref confirmed: Parks et al., "GTDB: an ongoing census of bacterial and archaeal diversity through a phylogenetically consistent, rank normalized and complete genome-based taxonomy", Nucleic Acids Research, R06-RS202 release. Bacterial tree contains 45,555 species clusters (matches claim exactly). Phylogeny inferred from 120 concatenated bacterial marker genes — every species cluster has direct genomic/molecular support (ANI clustering of sequenced genomes), no taxonomic-only imputation. Tree is divergence-based, not time-calibrated (no chronogram). GTDB is its own pipeline, independent of Open Tree of Life. Confidence=high: Crossref confirmed, abstract+article body read, all fields extractable.

Crossref confirmed: Parks et al., "GTDB release 10: a complete and systematic taxonomy for 715,230 bacterial and 17,245 archaeal genomes," Nucleic Acids Research, 2025 (online), 2026 (print). 715,230 bacterial genomes organized into 136,646 bacterial species clusters (matches claimed ntips exactly). Tree is NOT time-calibrated — phylogenetic topology only, built via concatenated marker gene trees with FastTree v2, with Relative Evolutionary Divergence (RED) used to define higher taxonomic ranks. molecular_tip_fraction=1.0: every species cluster is defined from actual genome sequences (no taxonomic placement / supertree grafting); the 86.9% "placeholder" figure refers to provisional Latin nomenclature, not absence of molecular data. ~70% of bacterial taxa are environmental MAGs/SAGs but still have full genome sequences. OTL involvement: none (GTDB is an independent genome-based taxonomy, not derived from OTL synthesis). Role: taxonomic-expansion is accurate — provides genome-derived topology to back-fill bacterial diversity not covered by dated chronograms. Gold OA, CC-BY.

Crossref DOI resolves and title/authors match exactly: 'A Phylogenomic Study of Birds Reveals Their Evolutionary History' (Hackett et al., Science 2008, 320:1763-1768). Abstract confirms 169 species sampled across all major extant avian groups, with ~32 kb of aligned nuclear sequence from 19 independent loci — every tip therefore has direct molecular support (molecular_tip_fraction=1.0). The paper itself reports an undated ML/Bayesian topology, not a time-calibrated chronogram (dated=false, dating_code=N); it became the canonical backbone subsequently used by Jetz et al. 2012 to build the first taxonomically complete dated bird tree (which would be the natural superseding canonical, hence reign_end_year=2012). No OTL synthesis involvement. Full-text not directly accessed (paywalled, Unpaywall reports closed access; journal landing page returned 403); fields are extracted from PubMed-hosted abstract plus the well-known published methodology, so confidence=medium.

Crossref-verified: title "The global diversity of birds in space and time" by Jetz, Thomas, Joy, Hartmann, Mooers, Nature 2012. The phylogeny includes all 9993 extant bird species. ~6670 species (66.7%) had direct molecular sequence support (genetic data backbone); the remaining ~3323 species (33.3%) were placed via taxonomic constraint (PASTIS-style taxonomic imputation) following the Upham 2019 strict type-1 convention. Dating via Bayesian relaxed clock (BEAST) with fossil calibrations. Trees distributed via BirdTree.org as a posterior distribution of 10000 trees. Widely used as the canonical bird phylogeny; available in Open Tree of Life as a collection-backed reference tree.

Crossref confirmed: 'A comprehensive phylogeny of birds (Aves) using targeted next-generation DNA sequencing' by Prum, Berv, Dornburg, Field, Townsend, E.M. Lemmon, A.R. Lemmon (Nature, 2015). 198 living bird species + 2 crocodilian outgroups, all sampled via anchored hybrid enrichment targeted next-gen sequencing (no taxonomic imputation; molecular_tip_fraction=1.0). Time-calibrated divergence-time analyses using Bayesian relaxed clock (BRC). No OTL pipeline involvement. Full text behind paywall; details extracted from Crossref metadata, abstract and TLDR summaries. Confidence=medium (abstract-level read, not full text PDF).

Crossref DOI resolved with exact title/author match: "Complexity of avian evolution revealed by family-level genomes" by Stiller, Feng, Chowdhury et al., Nature 2024. Abstract confirms genomes of 363 bird species (218 taxonomic families, 92% of total) — matches claimed ntips exactly. ERDA data repository (erda.ku.dk) explicitly contains "Time trees" directory, confirming time-calibrated chronograms ship with the paper (dated=true). The abstract describes sharp increases in substitution rates and population size after the K-Pg boundary, requiring a time-calibrated framework. All 363 tips have direct whole-genome data (this is a family-level phylogenomic effort using intergenic regions and coalescent methods), so molecular_tip_fraction=1.0 under Upham 2019 strict type-1 convention. No taxonomic placement / supertree grafting. No OTL pipeline involvement — this is a primary phylogenomic study, not a synthesis. Dating method (dating_code=BRC) assigned as Bayesian relaxed clock based on standard B10K-consortium practice (MCMCTree typically used for genome-scale avian dating), though the abstract itself does not specify the method; the full methods section was paywalled.

Crossref-confirmed: 'A complete and dynamic tree of birds', PNAS 2025, McTavish et al. Full paper text accessed via PMC12067227. Tip count of 10,824 matches the Clements 2021 taxonomy version (range 10,824-11,017 across taxonomy versions). 9,239 species (~85.4%) have direct molecular/phylogenetic data from 281 curated trees in 262 studies; remaining ~1,585 species placed via addTaxa taxonomic-placement algorithm using curated taxonomic constraints. Trees are time-scaled: 120 trees from 90 studies provide dates for ~63% of internal nodes; undated nodes interpolated via BLADJ-style penalized-likelihood spacing between dated parent/child nodes; summarized via RevBayes MCC. Synthesis uses the Open Tree of Life pipeline explicitly (custom synthesis with Open Tree synthesis software / propinquity), making this full-pipeline OTL involvement. Role 'taxonomic-expansion' is consistent with the addTaxa workflow.

Exact ntips=73 not directly verified from full text but consistent with a backbone Bivalvia sampling. Role as genomic-backbone-replacement is appropriate. No OTL pipeline involvement (independent phylogenomic study).

Crossref DOI resolves and title/authors match: Bechteler et al. 2023, 'Comprehensive phylogenomic time tree of bryophytes reveals deep relationships and uncovers gene incongruences in the last 500 million years of diversification', American Journal of Botany 110(11). No Open Tree of Life pipeline involvement; species tree from ASTRAL-III + RAxML concatenated ML.

Crossref-verified: 'A phylogeny of extant coleoid cephalopods with brain data', Basava et al., bioRxiv 2024-05-02 (v2 2024-05-05). Exact dating software not extractable from abstract; full text returned HTTP 403 from bioRxiv. Molecular tip fraction estimated at ~0.7 — many but not all of the 79 species likely have direct GenBank sequences; the rest are placed by taxonomy from prior literature. No Open Tree of Life pipeline mentioned. Recommend confirming ntips=79 and downgrading the claimed 81.

Matches the claimed 234 scleractinian tips for the Cnidaria/corals partition.

Tree is NOT time-calibrated — branch lengths fitted post-hoc; dating_code=ST (supertree). No Open Tree of Life pipeline involvement.

Crossref-verified: "The future of evolutionary diversity in reef corals", Huang & Roy 2015, Phil Trans B 370(1662):20140010. Paper is closed access (Unpaywall is_oa=false); journal landing page returned 403. The Huang & Roy supertree is built by grafting taxonomically-placed species onto a molecular backbone (the Huang 2012 molecular phylogeny covered ~535 species with sequence data; 1547 is reached via taxonomic placement of unsampled species). Time-calibration is by combining published clade-level chronograms (supertree-of-chronograms = ST). molecular_tip_fraction~0.35 is the best evidence-backed estimate (535/1547). No Open Tree of Life pipeline involvement. role=taxonomic-expansion is consistent with the methodology. Confidence=medium because abstract/citations were read but full methods text could not be retrieved.

Crossref confirmed: 'Palaeoclimate ocean conditions shaped the evolution of corals and their skeletons through deep time', Nature Ecology & Evolution 2020, Quattrini et al. Full text obtained from faircloth-lab.org PDF. The paper constructs a time-calibrated phylogeny of 234 anthozoans using 1,729 UCE loci captured via target enrichment with the PHYLUCE pipeline. Includes representatives from all orders and most families. Topology from RAxML on 50% data matrix (933 loci, 278,819 bp); ASTRAL III species tree as alternative. Divergence dating performed in BEAST2 v2.5 on CIPRES with 6 fossil calibrations and relaxed clock model (25 clock-like loci selected via SortaDate). A penalized-likelihood pre-step (ape) was used to initialize the fixed topology, but the published dated tree is the BEAST2 MCC tree; primary dating code is BRC. All tips are molecular (UCE sequence data) — no taxonomic imputation; molecular_tip_fraction = 1.0. No use of Open Tree of Life synthesis. Note: study is anthozoan-focused (corals + sea anemones); 'Cnidaria' partition naming includes some Medusozoa outgroups in Extended Data Fig. 5 but the canonical phylogeny is the 234-tip anthozoan tree. Claimed ntips (234) and genomic-backbone-replacement role both confirmed.

All-molecular phylogeny with no OTL/supertree grafting reported; molecular_tip_fraction set to 1.0 under Upham 2019 strict type-1 convention. Confidence=medium because Crossref confirmed and abstract read, but full Methods section not directly accessible.

Crossref confirmed: Jamie R. Oaks, "A TIME-CALIBRATED SPECIES TREE OF CROCODYLIA REVEALS A RECENT RADIATION OF THE TRUE CROCODILES," Evolution 65(11):3285, 2011. study_label: Bracken et al. 2009 - The Decapod Tree of Life
notes: Crossref DOI resolves and matches the proposed study (Bracken, Toon, Felder, Martin, Finley, Rasmussen, Palero, Crandall 2009; Arthropod Systematics & Phylogeny 67(1):99-116). Per the abstract and prior literature, the molecular phylogeny used 62 decapod species across 22 genera (2 mtDNA + 6 nuclear markers: 12S, 16S, ATPsβ, enolase, GAPDH, H3, PEPCK, NaK ATPase α). Proposed ntips of 69 likely reflects an OTL-mapped version with outgroups or higher counts after taxonomy reconciliation; actual tip count in the original paper is 62. The paper aimed at higher-level systematic consensus rather than divergence-time estimation; Bayesian topology (MrBayes) without time-calibration in this paper itself (divergence-time work was done in a sister paper Bracken et al. 2010 Zoologica Scripta). All tips have direct molecular sequence support (no taxonomic placement / supertree grafting), so molecular_tip_fraction=1.0. Full PDF could not be retrieved (Pensoft PDF endpoint redirects to a tokenized URL); evidence taken from Crossref, the journal landing page, and the web search summary of the paper's abstract/methods.

Crossref confirmed: 'The Emergence of Lobsters: Phylogenetic Relationships, Morphological Evolution and Divergence Time Comparisons of an Ancient Group (Decapoda: Achelata, Astacidea, Glypheidea, Polychelida)' by Bracken-Grissom et al. (Sys Bio 2014). Abstract confirms 173 species (not the claimed 142 — claim may reflect a subset, e.g., taxa with complete molecular data) across all major lobster families. Time-calibrated tree using six molecular markers (mitochondrial + nuclear) plus morphology, with Bayesian fossil-calibrated divergence-time estimation. Note: the paper covers lobsters (infraorders Polychelida, Glypheidea, Astacidea, Achelata) — only a portion of Decapoda, not the entire order. This is a clade-level study, not a Decapoda-wide tree; if the partition is 'Decapoda' broadly, the paper covers only ~4 of ~10 infraorders and may not be the ideal canonical. Methodological-update role is plausible if it superseded an earlier tip-count-richer but methodologically weaker phylogeny. Full methods text not directly extracted (paywalled); confidence=medium based on abstract.

Crossref DOI resolved; title 'A phylogenomic framework, evolutionary timeline and genomic resources for comparative studies of decapod crustaceans' and authors (Wolfe, Breinholt, Crandall, Lemmon, Lemmon, Timm, Siddall, Bracken-Grissom) match the proposed study.
